$comment: Hand-written half of the IPC method descriptors. Parameters, types, defaults and capabilities are extracted from the dispatch code by gen_ipc_descriptors.py - do NOT repeat them here unless you are adding a description, an enum hint or correcting a type the parser could only see as 'any'. Keys: summary (required, one line, present tense), notes, tags (extra search synonyms; the domain and the method name are added automatically), related (pipe-separated), returns, undoable, access, params{name:{description,enum,type,required,default}}.

agent.discover.summary: Identify the application and list every capability domain, agent role and coverage metric
agent.discover.notes: First call for a new agent session. registered_methods is how many methods are dispatched; documented_coverage is the share that carries a hand-written summary. A documented_coverage below 1.0 means agent.describe will answer some methods with parameters but no explanation.

agent.list_methods.summary: List every registered IPC method, optionally filtered to one domain
agent.list_methods.notes: The full list is around 30 KB. Cache it once per session instead of calling it per step.

domain.description: Domain to restrict the listing to, e.g. 'fluid'. Omit for every method.

agent.describe.summary: Return the full parameter schema, capability and related methods for one IPC method
agent.describe.notes: Parameters come from the dispatch code itself, so they are exact. `documented: false` means the schema is real but nobody has written the prose yet - trust the parameters, be careful with intent.

agent.search_capabilities.summary: Search workflow recipes and method metadata for a plain-language goal
agent.search_capabilities.notes: Recipes are the valuable half: each one is an ordered list of calls that is known to work end to end. Prefer following a recipe over assembling calls from the method hits.

query.description: Plain language goal, e.g. 'make a wooden object burn'

agent.get_examples.summary: Return runnable call sequences for a method or a named workflow recipe

method.description: Method to show examples for, e.g. 'fluid.create_domain'

agent.get_state_summary.summary: Compact snapshot of scene, lights, camera, timeline and viewport measurement state
agent.get_state_summary.notes: The viewport block is a MEASUREMENT and is only present when frame capture is on and a frame exists; when it is absent that means 'not measured', never 'measured zero'. Turn capture on with viewport.capture before relying on it.

include_probe.description: Sample the last viewport frame for luminance and black/NaN fractions. Costs a full-frame scan.

agent.roles.summary: Describe the manager/controller/worker agent roles and their delegation chain
agent.roles.notes: Informational only. Access is decided by the security capability on the connection token, not by the role an agent claims.

agent.chat_send.summary: Post a message into the Studio Agent Chat panel
agent.chat_send.notes: This WRITES to the user interface, so it needs the AgentChat capability - it is the one agent.* method that is not read-only. Use type='activity' for per-call progress, 'thought' for reasoning, 'error' for failures; the panel colours and filters them separately.

sender.description: Display name shown in the panel, e.g. 'RayTrophi Agent'

payload.description: Optional structured data appended to the message

image_base64.description: Optional base64 image; the panel notes the attachment

agent.send_prompt.summary: Queue a task for another agent to pick up on its next poll, addressed by agent id or 'all'
agent.send_prompt.notes: Returns queued:true, NOT delivered - nothing has run yet and the target agent may never poll. Do not report the work as done on the strength of this call; ask for the result, or check the scene yourself. The target must match the id the other agent polls with (agent.chat_poll agent_id), and 'all' broadcasts.

agent.chat_poll.summary: Take the user prompts queued in the Agent Chat panel and mark the agent as alive
agent.chat_poll.notes: Polling is also the panel's heartbeat: it shows the agent as online for a few seconds after each call. An agent that blocks on a long model turn should keep polling from a second thread, or the panel reports it offline.

version.summary: Return the RayTrophi Studio version string

batch.summary: Execute several IPC calls in order and return one result array
batch.notes: Each child call is authorized on its own; nesting a batch inside a batch is refused. A failing child does not stop the rest.

undo.summary: Undo the last recorded scene command

redo.summary: Redo the last undone scene command

undo_description.summary: Name of the command that undo would revert

redo_description.summary: Name of the command that redo would reapply

request_render.summary: Ask the viewport to render another frame

reset_accumulation.summary: Restart progressive sample accumulation in the viewport
reset_accumulation.notes: Post-process changes must NOT reset accumulation - only changes to scene, camera or lighting should.

scene.list_objects.summary: List every object in the scene by name
scene.list_objects.notes: Covers both flat SoA meshes and legacy facade objects, so it is the reliable inventory call.

scene.object_exists.summary: Report whether an object with this name exists

scene.object_info.summary: Return vertex and triangle counts for one object

scene.add_primitive.summary: Create a primitive mesh object and return its final name
scene.add_primitive.notes: The name is made unique by suffix, so the returned name may differ from the requested one - always use the returned name afterwards.

name.description: Requested name; a numeric suffix is added if it is taken

size.description: Edge length or radius in metres; must be positive

scene.delete.summary: Delete an object from the scene

scene.duplicate.summary: Duplicate an object and return the new object's name

scene.get_transform.summary: Return an object's translation, rotation, scale and full matrix
scene.get_transform.notes: This is the AUTHORED transform and a solver never writes it: a rigid body can fall for a thousand steps while this keeps returning the spawn pose. To measure physics use scene.get_world_transform.

scene.get_world_transform.summary: Return an object's SIMULATED world pose: the solver's motion composed onto the authored transform
scene.get_world_transform.notes: The rigid solver bakes its motion into the mesh vertices and never writes a transform, so scene.get_transform reports the spawn pose for a body that has been falling for hundreds of steps. Every physics measurement - free fall, buoyancy draft, restitution, settling - has to read this one. The result carries simulated: false when no solver has contributed, which is not the same as the body having stayed still.

scene.set_transform.summary: Set an object's transform, either as a matrix or as translation/rotation/scale components
scene.set_transform.notes: Send `matrix`, or any combination of translation/rotation/scale - components you omit keep their current value. Rotation is in degrees.

matrix.description: Row-major 4x4 matrix; wins over the component form when both are sent

scene.import_model.summary: Import a model file (glTF/FBX/OBJ) into the scene

select.object.summary: Select an object by name, optionally adding to the current selection

select.light.summary: Select a light by index, optionally adding to the current selection

select.deselect_object.summary: Remove one object from the selection

select.all_objects.summary: Select every object in the scene

select.list.summary: List the currently selected objects and lights

camera.get.summary: Return camera position, target, up vector, field of view, focus distance and aperture

camera.set_position.summary: Move the camera to a world position

camera.set_target.summary: Aim the camera at a world position

camera.set_fov.summary: Set the camera field of view in degrees

camera.set_focus_distance.summary: Set the depth-of-field focus distance in metres

camera.set_aperture.summary: Set the camera aperture; larger values give shallower depth of field

lights.list.summary: List the scene lights with index, name, type and position

lights.get.summary: Return every property of one light

lights.add.summary: Add a light of the given type at a world position and return its name

lights.set_position.summary: Move a light to a world position

lights.set_direction.summary: Set the direction a directional or spot light points in

lights.set_visible.summary: Show or hide a light without deleting it

lights.set_param.summary: Set one numeric light parameter by name (radius, spot_angle, spot_falloff, width, height)
lights.set_param.notes: spot_angle and spot_falloff apply to spot lights only; width and height to area lights only. The call fails rather than silently ignoring a mismatch.

param.description: Which light property to set. Not every key applies to every light type - a key the light does not have is refused, not ignored.

world.get.summary: Return world mode, background colour, sun angles and atmosphere settings

world.set_mode.summary: Switch the world background between flat colour, HDRI and physical sky

world.set_background_color.summary: Set the flat background colour used in solid world mode

world.set_sun_elevation.summary: Set the sun elevation angle of the physical sky

world.set_sun_azimuth.summary: Set the sun compass angle of the physical sky

world.set_sun_intensity.summary: Set the sun intensity of the physical sky

world.set_sun_size.summary: Set the sun's angular size; larger values give softer shadows

world.set_atmosphere_intensity.summary: Set the strength of atmospheric scattering in the physical sky

world.get_thermal.summary: Return the ambient thermal condition every uncoupled substance relaxes toward
world.get_thermal.notes: Distinct from world.get: that is the render sky, this is WorldThermalState -- the room temperature (ambient_kelvin), the Kelvin-per-normalized-unit calibration a substance's MSF temperature is read against (kelvin_per_unit), the passive-cooling multiplier (convection_coefficient) and the pyrolysis rate scale (oxygen_availability). Formerly no scripting surface existed for any of this -- see docs/dev/SIMULATION_NODE_OBJECT_MODEL.md section 7 item 1.

world.set_thermal.summary: Set the ambient thermal condition every uncoupled substance relaxes toward
world.set_thermal.notes: Every field optional: omit a key to leave it unchanged. oxygen_availability is clamped to 0..1 rather than rejected. A domain's own thermal_override_enabled (SimulationGridDomainDesc) still wins over this where it is set -- this call changes only the default a domain has not overridden.

ambient_kelvin.description: Room temperature everything relaxes toward, in Kelvin. Must be positive.

kelvin_per_unit.description: Kelvin per normalized solver unit -- the calibration MSF temperature reads through. Must be positive.

convection_coefficient.description: Scales every substance's passive cooling toward ambient: 1 = authored, higher = draughty, 0 = a perfect thermos.

oxygen_availability.description: 0..1, scales pyrolysis burn rate; 0 smothers combustion entirely. Clamped, not rejected, if out of range.

timeline.set_frame.summary: Move the timeline playhead to a frame
timeline.set_frame.notes: This is how simulations are advanced from a script: stepping the frame runs the solvers that are live for that frame.

render.start.summary: Render one frame at the given sample count and write it to an image file
render.start.notes: Blocking work runs on the render job; poll render.status for progress. The written image can be read back, so visual checks can be automated.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the image file to write

render.start_sequence.summary: Render a frame range to an output directory

render.status.summary: Report render job state, progress and current sample count

render.sequence_status.summary: Report sequence render progress and current frame

render.probe.summary: Measure a region of the last viewport frame: mean/min/max luminance, black fraction, NaN fraction and a histogram
render.probe.notes: This is the measurement an agent verifies its own work with. `available: false` means no frame was captured - it is not a dark scene. A non-zero nan_fraction means a shader produced invalid pixels.

width.description: Region width in pixels; 0 means to the right edge

height.description: Region height in pixels; 0 means to the bottom edge

threshold.description: Luminance at or below which a pixel counts as black

render.volume_stats.summary: Return volume traversal counters for the last frame

render.volume_counters.summary: Enable or disable volume instrumentation counters

viewport.status.summary: Report viewport backend, shading mode, resolution, sample count, capture state and whether a frame is available

viewport.shading.summary: Report which viewport shading mode is on screen and whether the interactive raster viewport exists
viewport.shading.notes: interactive_available false means this build has no raster viewport (no Vulkan), so 'rendered' is the only selectable mode - a rejected viewport.set_shading there is the machine, not a bad request.

viewport.get_screenshot.summary: Return the captured viewport frame as a base64 JPEG, for a vision-capable model to look at
viewport.get_screenshot.notes: Requires viewport.capture(enabled=true) and at least one rendered frame; an empty result means NOT CAPTURED, never 'the screen is empty'. Looking is not measuring - pair it with render.probe when the question is numeric (is there a black band, did the frame change), because a model reading a JPEG cannot tell 0.001 luminance from 0.

viewport.set_shading.summary: Switch the viewport shading mode (solid, material, rendered, matcap) and optionally the matcap preset
viewport.set_shading.notes: Resets accumulation like the panel buttons do, so probe AFTER switching - otherwise you measure the frame from the mode you left. Fails loudly when a mode is unavailable instead of silently falling back to rendered.

mode.description: Canonical mode name. 'preview' is accepted as an alias for material because the panel button reads Preview.

matcap_preset.description: 0..9, meaningful in matcap mode; -1 leaves it unchanged.

viewport.capture.summary: Turn viewport frame capture on or off
viewport.capture.notes: Capture must be on before render.probe or the state summary can measure anything.

viewport.render_frames.summary: Render a fixed number of viewport frames and report timing and convergence
viewport.render_frames.notes: Use this to converge the viewport deliberately before probing it, instead of guessing how long to wait. Over IPC the captured frame is refreshed between calls by the display loop, so viewport.capture -> viewport.render_frames -> render.probe works. It does NOT work inside a single script.run_file: the script holds the main thread, the display loop never runs, and viewport.status frame_available stays false however many frames were rendered - measured 2026-08-19.

material.list.summary: List every material in the scene

material.create.summary: Create a material of the given type and return its name

material.assign.summary: Assign an existing material to an object

material.info.summary: Return a material's full parameter set

material.of_object.summary: List the materials used by one object

material.get.summary: Read one material parameter of an object

material.set.summary: Set one material parameter on an object (base_color, roughness, metallic, emission, ior, transmission, ...)
material.set.notes: Colour parameters take a 3-element array, scalars take a number. An unknown parameter name is an error, not a silent no-op.

param.description: Which Principled BSDF property to set. Colour keys (base_color, emission, resin_color, dust_color_a/b, resin_dirt_color) need an RGB value; the rest need a scalar. roughness, metallic, specular, transmission and opacity are clamped to [0,1]; ior to [1,10].

material.set_texture.summary: Bind an image file to a material texture slot

material.textures.summary: List a material's texture slots and their bound files

fluid.create_domain.summary: Create an APIC liquid or gas grid domain over a world-space box
fluid.create_domain.notes: voxel_size sets both resolution and cost: halving it multiplies cell count by eight. A liquid domain does nothing until fluid.seed or a flow_source fills it. Changing voxel_size later invalidates the bake.

name.description: Domain name; also the object name in the scene

voxel_size.description: Grid cell size in metres. Drives resolution, cost and the smallest feature the solver can resolve.

fluid.list_domains.summary: List every fluid and gas domain with its full settings

fluid.get.summary: Return one fluid or gas domain's complete settings and live counters

fluid.remove_domain.summary: Delete a fluid or gas domain

fluid.seed.summary: Fill a liquid domain with particles - a given box, or the domain's lower half
fluid.seed.notes: Omit seed_min and seed_max to fill the bottom half of the domain; there is no fixed default box any more, because the old one was derived from nothing and seeded zero particles in any domain that did not contain it. A region that does not overlap the domain is now refused with both boxes in the error, instead of succeeding having created nothing. particles_per_cell of 4 is the standard APIC density; a thin jet seeded below that has no interior cells and therefore no pressure field, which reads as 'water that will not splash'. persistent=true re-seeds the box every reset.

seed_min.description: World-space box minimum in metres; omit to derive from the domain

seed_max.description: World-space box maximum in metres; omit to derive from the domain

particles_per_cell.description: Particle density per grid cell; 4 is standard

persistent.description: Re-apply this seed after every reset

fluid.clear.summary: Remove the particles from a fluid domain

fluid.reset.summary: Reset every fluid and gas simulation to frame zero

fluid.step.summary: Advance the fluid solver by one timestep
fluid.step.notes: For scripted work prefer timeline.set_frame, which advances every solver consistently.

fluid.set_param.summary: Update any field of a fluid or gas domain: bounds, voxel size, solver backend, viscosity, granular constitutive settings, render mode and surface material
fluid.set_param.notes: Overlay semantics - fields you do not send keep their value. Changing voxel_size or the bounds invalidates the bake for that domain.

fluid.set_substance_material.summary: Bind a substance (its physical identity, phase and representation) to a fluid domain
fluid.set_substance_material.notes: Phase is what the matter IS; representation is how it is solved and drawn. They are separate axes - setting one does not imply the other.

representation.description: How the substance is solved and rendered

fluid.set_splat_material.summary: Set the material used for particle splat rendering of a domain

fluid.get_combustion.summary: Read a liquid domain's combustion settings

fluid.set_combustion.summary: Configure a liquid domain as a combustible fuel: ignition temperature, heat release, smoke yield and evaporation

gas.create_domain.summary: Create a gas grid domain over a world-space box
gas.create_domain.notes: Same handler as fluid.create_domain with type defaulting to gas.

gas.list_domains.summary: List every gas and fluid domain with its settings

gas.get.summary: Return one gas domain's complete settings and live counters

gas.get_settings.summary: Read a gas domain's solver settings: fire, buoyancy, turbulence, quality and resource budget

gas.set_settings.summary: Configure a gas domain's solver: fire and ignition, burn rate, heat release, buoyancy, turbulence, vorticity and resource budget
gas.set_settings.notes: This is the SOLVER. Appearance - colour, emission, density scale - lives in gas.set_shader, and the two are read back separately; a fire that simulates but looks wrong is usually a shader setting, not a solver setting.

ignition_temperature.description: Temperature at which fuel ignites, in Kelvin

burn_rate.description: How fast fuel is consumed once lit

heat_release.description: Temperature added per unit of fuel burned

smoke_generation.description: Smoke produced per unit of fuel burned

gas.get_shader.summary: Read a gas domain's volume shading settings

gas.set_shader.summary: Set a gas domain's volume appearance: preset, density and absorption/scattering, blackbody emission and the temperature range it maps
gas.set_shader.notes: temperature_min/max define the window mapped to emission colour; a flame outside that window renders black however hot it is.

gas.set_param.summary: Update any field of a gas domain (same overlay setter as fluid.set_param)

gas.step.summary: Advance the gas solver by one timestep

gas.reset.summary: Reset every gas and fluid simulation to frame zero

gas.pressure_pulse.summary: Inject a pressure pulse into a gas domain, as an explosion or blast wave

gas.structural_impulse_stats.summary: Report the blast impulses the gas solver handed to the structural/fracture side

flow_source.create.summary: Create an emitter that feeds a fluid or gas domain with mass, heat, fuel or particles
flow_source.create.notes: An emitter belongs to a domain by name. With a parent_object it follows that object, and velocity_space decides whether its velocity is read in world or parent-local space.

domain.description: Target fluid or gas domain name

source_object.description: Object whose surface or volume emits

velocity.description: Emitted velocity in metres per second

velocity_space.description: Frame the velocity is expressed in

fluid_substance.description: Substance id emitted into a liquid domain

flow_source.update.summary: Update fields of an existing emitter, keeping everything you do not send
flow_source.update.notes: Read-modify-write on purpose: sending only one field must not reset the rest.

flow_source.list.summary: List every emitter with its settings

msf.substances.summary: List the material substance library: every substance an object or fluid can be made of
msf.substances.notes: Substance ids from here are what fluid.set_substance_material and the combustion path expect.

msf.fields.summary: Report the live material state fields (temperature, moisture, char, mass) per object
msf.fields.notes: This is the measurement side of burning and melting: mass loss, integrity and mass-conservation error are reported here.

physics.add_body.summary: Give an object a rigid-body with a mass, motion type and collision shape

shape.description: Collision shape, e.g. box, sphere, mesh

physics.get_body.summary: Return a rigid body's mass, damping, friction, restitution and motion type

physics.set_gravity.summary: Set the world gravity vector in metres per second squared

physics.step.summary: Advance the physics solver by dt and move the playhead with it
physics.step.notes: Advances the solver AND the timeline playhead, and claims the timeline until the user scrubs, plays or stops. It used to advance only the solver: the playhead stayed put, the frame loop found a rigid state that disagreed with the displayed frame, and it reset the runtime to the rest pose - erasing every scripted step while this call returned success. Check sim.control_state around a measurement to learn whether the claim was taken back.

physics.reset.summary: Reset the rigid-body simulation to its initial state

physics.fracture_object.summary: Shatter an object into Voronoi shards and return the shard objects
physics.fracture_object.notes: site_count sets how many shards; exact_surface clips shards against the real surface instead of approximating it. The shards are ordinary objects afterwards - group them with physics.make_fracture_group so they hold together until something breaks them.

site_count.description: Number of Voronoi sites, i.e. shards

cluster_count.description: Number of shard clusters to form

exact_surface.description: Clip shards against the exact surface rather than an approximation

preview_gap.description: Visual gap between shards in metres, for preview only

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible shard layouts

physics.unfracture_object.summary: Restore a fractured object back to its unbroken form

physics.make_fracture_group.summary: Bond shards into a fracture group that holds together until the break threshold is exceeded
physics.make_fracture_group.notes: break_velocity is a velocity threshold, not an impulse - the group's mass is taken into account when the threshold is evaluated.

physics.break_fracture_group.summary: Break a fracture group apart immediately with a given strength

physics.apply_fracture_impulse.summary: Apply an impulse at a point on a fracture group and report whether it broke

physics.get_fracture_group.summary: Report a fracture group's mass, integrity and break thresholds

physics.fracture_cluster_groups.summary: List or build the cluster groups of a fractured object

forcefield.create.summary: Create a force field of the given type and return its name

forcefield.list.summary: List the force fields in the scene

forcefield.get.summary: Return one force field's full settings

forcefield.set_param.summary: Update a force field: shape, strength, falloff, noise, drag and which solvers it affects
forcefield.set_param.notes: A force field is spatial - it is NOT attached to a domain. Which solvers feel it is decided by the affects_* flags.

forcefield.evaluate.summary: Evaluate the combined force fields at a world position and return the resulting acceleration
forcefield.evaluate.notes: The way to check a field really reaches a place, rather than inferring it from how a simulation looks.

particle.list_systems.summary: List the particle systems with their emitter, domain and collider counts

particle.get_emitter.summary: Return one particle emitter's full settings

particle.add_emitter.summary: Add a particle emitter and return it

particle.set_emitter.summary: Update fields of a particle emitter, keeping what you do not send

particle.clear.summary: Delete the live particles without touching the emitters

particle.spawn.summary: Spawn one particle with an explicit position, velocity, size, mass and lifetime

particle.set_physics.summary: Set the particle solver: mode, quality, rest density, viscosity, cohesion, self-collision and grid deposit rates

particle.stats.summary: Report live particle counts and per-stage solver timings

particle.step.summary: Advance the particle solver by one timestep

terrain.get.summary: Return one terrain's size, resolution, height scale and node-graph state

terrain.create.summary: Create a terrain heightfield of a given world size and resolution

resolution.description: Heightmap resolution in samples per side

terrain.create.notes: resolution is the FIELD grid: heights and every analysis product (slope, flow, erosion, analysisFields) live at that resolution. mesh_resolution is the separate VERTEX grid; 0 follows the field. Set it at creation rather than decimating afterwards - creating at 4096 and decimating still pays one full-resolution acceleration-structure build (measured 5.6 s Vulkan solid raster + 2.8 s Embree). With a 1024 mesh over a 4096 field the same build is 0.42 s + 0.15 s.

terrain.apply_preset.summary: Apply a built-in terrain node preset

add_satmap.description: Also add and wire a matching SatMap colorizer

terrain.list_satmap_presets.summary: List data-driven multi-field SatMap preset recipes

terrain.apply_satmap_preset.summary: Build a SatMap node recipe from flow, slope, curvature and other terrain fields

terrain.erode.summary: Run an erosion pass over a terrain

iterations.description: Solver iterations; 0 uses the model's own default

backend.description: Compute backend; auto picks GPU when available

terrain.evaluate.summary: Evaluate the terrain node graph and bake the result into the heightfield

terrain.evaluation_status.summary: Report terrain evaluation progress and the node being processed

terrain.sample_height.summary: Sample terrain height at a world position

terrain.carve_river.summary: Carve a river channel along a path into the terrain

terrain.list_rivers.summary: List the rivers carved into a terrain

terrain.calculate_flow.summary: Compute the water flow map over a terrain

terrain.import_heightmap.summary: Import a heightmap image into a terrain

terrain.export_heightmap.summary: Export a terrain heightfield to an image file

scatter.list_groups.summary: List the scatter groups with their sources, counts and placement settings

scatter.create_group.summary: Create a scatter group that instances objects over a target surface

scatter.add_source.summary: Add a source object that a scatter group may instance

scatter.fill.summary: Populate a scatter group and report how many instances were spawned

scatter.clear.summary: Remove the instances of a scatter group, keeping the group

hair.get.summary: Return one hair groom's full settings

hair.create.summary: Create a hair groom bound to a mesh

hair.update.summary: Update hair groom settings, keeping what you do not send

hair.grow.summary: Scale hair length by a factor

hair.comb.summary: Comb hair strands towards a direction with a root stiffness

hair.apply_preset.summary: Apply a built-in hair preset to a groom

hair.bake.summary: Bake a hair groom to its cached geometry

hair.reset_simulation.summary: Reset hair dynamics to the rest pose

paint.ensure.summary: Create or return the paint target (texture set) for an object

paint.get.summary: Return an object's paint target: layers, channels and resolution

paint.add_layer.summary: Add a paint layer to an object's texture set

paint.move_layer.summary: Reorder a paint layer in the stack

paint.update_layer.summary: Set a paint layer's name, opacity, blend mode, visibility or lock

paint.merge_down.summary: Merge a paint layer into the one below it

paint.flatten.summary: Flatten every paint layer into one

paint.fill.summary: Fill a paint layer channel with a value or colour

paint.clear_channel.summary: Clear one channel of a paint layer

paint.apply_mask.summary: Apply a mask preset to a paint layer

paint.list_mask_presets.summary: List the available paint mask presets

paint.bake_height_to_normal.summary: Bake a paint height channel into the normal channel

paint.import_channel.summary: Import an image into a paint layer channel

paint.export_channel.summary: Export a paint layer channel to an image file

sculpt.get.summary: Report an object's sculpt state: vertex count and mask range

sculpt.stroke.summary: Apply a sculpt brush stroke to a mesh

sculpt.paint_mask.summary: Paint the sculpt mask on a mesh

sculpt.mask_operation.summary: Run an operation over the sculpt mask (invert, clear, grow, ...)

modifiers.add.summary: Add a modifier to an object and return the new stack entry

modifiers.remove.summary: Remove a modifier from an object

modifiers.apply.summary: Apply a modifier destructively into the mesh

modifiers.set_param.summary: Set a modifier parameter: enabled, levels, render_levels or smooth_angle

nodes.graphs.summary: List the node graphs that exist

nodes.create_graph.summary: Create a node graph in a domain

nodes.types.summary: List every node type with its category and description

nodes.list.summary: List the nodes of a graph with their inputs and outputs

nodes.add.summary: Add a node of the given type to a graph

nodes.remove.summary: Remove a node from a graph

nodes.link.summary: Connect one node's output to another node's input

nodes.list_params.summary: List a node's parameters, their types, values and whether they are driven by a link

nodes.apply.summary: Evaluate a node graph and apply its result, reporting errors and warnings

sim_graph.list.summary: List the simulation node graphs with their scope, owner and whether the owner still exists
sim_graph.list.notes: owner_missing means the graph outlived the entity it was written for - it will not run.

sim_graph.create.summary: Create a simulation node graph for a scope and owner
sim_graph.create.notes: Scope and owner are mandatory and identify what the graph drives; a graph is not global.

sim_graph.clear.summary: Remove every node from a simulation graph

sim_graph.nodes.summary: List a simulation graph's nodes, their channels, sources and restart requirements

sim_graph.add_node.summary: Add a node of the given type to a simulation graph

sim_graph.connect.summary: Connect two nodes in a simulation graph

sim_graph.set_node.summary: Set a text-valued key on a simulation node

sim.control_state.summary: Who is currently driving the solvers, and an epoch that changes whenever anything re-poses them
sim.control_state.notes: Read epoch before and after a measurement. If it changed, the solvers were re-posed under you - the user scrubbed, playback ran, or a reset fired - and the numbers you just read are not a physics result. Without this a reverted pose and a body that never moved read exactly the same. driver says which of those it was; script_driving is true while physics.step holds the timeline, which it keeps only until the user scrubs, plays or stops.
